title: Long bash-approval option text overflows the terminal edge uncut on a narrow (60-col) window instead of wrapping or truncating with …
observed: At 60x30, option 3 reads ' 3  Yes, and switch to auto mode · auto mode handles these p' (01-bash-prompt-60-cols.txt) — hard-clipped mid-word at the terminal's right edge with no '…' and no wrap to a second line, unlike the same text at 120 cols where it fits on one line, and unlike edit/write prompts' option 2 which wraps onto a continuation line ('session (shift+tab)') when it doesn't fit.
expected: Option rows should wrap or truncate with an ellipsis like other kiln text, not silently overflow past the terminal width.
design_ref: internal/tui/permission_render.go: RenderBashPermissionPrompt (around line 171) builds and returns its lines directly with no FitLines/FitStatus call, unlike the generic feedback-prompt path in the same file (lines 105,116: return FitLines(lines, width, "    ")) — the bash prompt's option rows are never wrapped or width-fitted
